jobs.title: Social Media & Content Manager (m/w/d), Vollzeit oder Teilzeit ab 20h, 100% Remote
jobs.description:
Du kommst aus NRW und hast Bock mit Social Media organische Reichweite aufzubauen, die direkten Einfluss auf unsere Performance hat? Du willst Kanäle nicht verwalten, sondern selbst bespielen, von der Idee bis zum fertigen Reel? Dann lies weiter.

Damit wir uns nicht missverstehen: Wir suchen keine reine Redaktionsplan-Verwaltung, die Content einplant, den jemand anderes produziert. Wir suchen jemanden, der unsere Kanäle in die Hand nimmt. Du suchst die Creatorinnen, du schreibst, was gedreht werden soll, du schneidest, du postest, du antwortest und du sprichst unsere Ads ein. Und du zeigst dich selbst: in unseren Stories, vor der Kamera, mit deiner Stimme. Wenn du lieber im Hintergrund bleibst, passt es nicht. Bei uns liegt Organic komplett bei dir.

Aufgaben

Du verantwortest unsere organische Präsenz, von der Idee bis zum fertigen Post. Sivara ist eine Damen-Unterwäsche- und Umstandsmode-Brand mit über 120.000 Kundinnen, unsere Community redet viel mit uns, und genau da entsteht dein Content.

Du bespielst Instagram und TikTok mit Reels, Stories und Posts, sodass wir präsent sind.

Du produzierst und schneidest selbst: aus Creator-Material und eigenen Aufnahmen baust du Videos, die unser Produkt richtig in Szene setzen.

Du betreust unsere Community auf Instagram und Facebook, beantwortest Kommentare und Nachrichten und erkennst dabei, welche Fragen immer wieder kommen. Aus genau diesen Fragen machst du dann Stories und Reels, die sie beantworten.

Du findest neue UGC-Creatorinnen, die zu uns passen, verhandelst Barter-Deals und arbeitest mit Plattformen wie Trybe, etc.

Du schreibst die Shootinglisten für unsere Creatorinnen, sammelst das Material ein und sortierst es so, dass wir damit arbeiten können.

Du stehst selbst vor der Kamera: eine Story aus deinem Alltag, ein spontanes Video aus dem Lager, eine Ansage an die Community. Und du wirkst bei unseren Ad-Creatives mit, wenn wir dich brauchen.

Du sprichst die Voice-Over für unsere Ads ein.

Du betreust unsere Affiliate- und Deal-Partner, findest neue Partner und baust den Kanal mit aus.

Du entwickelst, wie unsere Kanäle klingen und aussehen, schaust dir an was funktioniert hat und was nicht, und planst den nächsten Monat danach.

Qualifikation

Erfahrung im Social Media Marketing oder in der Content-Produktion, idealerweise für eine Brand oder im E-Commerce.

Du schneidest selbst und sicher, mit CapCut, Premiere oder einem vergleichbaren Tool.

Du hast eine angenehme, natürliche Sprechstimme und Lust darauf, regelmäßig Voice-Over einzusprechen.

Du bist extrovertiert und stehst gerne selbst vor der Kamera. In die Kamera sprechen, ins Mikro sprechen, dich in unseren Stories mit deinem Gesicht zeigen, ist für dich kein Problem.

Du erkennst Formate und Trends früh und probierst sie aus, statt darauf zu warten, dass jemand sie freigibt.

Du triffst im Community Management den richtigen Ton, freundlich und auf Augenhöhe, auch wenn eine Kundin genervt schreibt.

Deutsch auf Muttersprach-Niveau, weil alles was du schreibst direkt bei unseren Kundinnen landet.

Du organisierst dich im Remote-Setup selbst und ziehst Themen durch, auch wenn niemand zuschaut.

Nice-to-have: erste Berührung mit Affiliate- oder Deal-Plattformen, Erfahrung im Verhandeln mit Creatorinnen und deren Managements.

Benefits

100% Remote, du arbeitest, wo du willst.

Flexible Arbeitszeiten, die sich deinem Leben anpassen. Wir bewerten dich nach Leistung, nicht nach Anwesenheit.

Arzttermine, Workation und Ähnliches sind bei uns unkompliziert möglich, kurze Absprache reicht.

Flache Hierarchien.

Performance-Bonus für echte Ergebnisse.

Netzwerk: Sivara ist eng vernetzt mit den führenden D2C-Brands Deutschlands und tauscht sich täglich mit anderen E-Commerce-Brands im 8- bis 9-stelligen Bereich aus. Du bekommst Einblicke und Kontakte, die du dir sonst über Jahre aufbauen müsstest.

Bis hier durch? Dann sind wir vielleicht dein Match.

Schick mir gerne ein kurzes, ungezwungenes Anschreiben per du. Was hast du bisher gemacht, welche Kanäle oder Accounts hast du selbst bespielt, was war dein bestes Video und warum hat es funktioniert, ab wann hättest du Lust, etc.

Bitte kein 5-Seiten-Roman mit "ich bin teamfähig und belastbar", sondern lieber kurz und knapp warum du perfekt geeignet bist und ggf. ein Portfolio-Link zu deiner bisherigen Arbeit.

Ich freu mich von dir zu hören!

Beste Grüße
Kacper

jobs.title: Staff/Senior Software Engineer - Hydris - Golang (d/f/m)
jobs.description:
New ChallengeAbout Us 
Project Q GmbH ("Q") is a Germany-based DefenseTech company with offices in Berlin and Munich. We network market-available sensors, effectors, or situational awareness systems into a tactical IoT backbone that reliably provides armed forces and security agencies with cross-domain information superiority — automated, scalable, and cost-efficient.

Our solutions integrate seamlessly into existing defense and maritime infrastructures, delivering fast data fusion and AI-enhanced analytics for robust situational awareness in dynamic environments. We build platform-agnostic systems that enable real interoperability across domains.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll directly impact the technical direction of our orchestration products – Hydris – the coordination engine for sensors and mission systems, and the interoperability API that underpins it. 

You'll work at the layer where heterogeneous real-world systems like radars, AIS receivers, LoRa mesh radios, satellite feeds, and C2 platforms become a single coherent picture. The problems lie in distributed systems, protocols, and data modeling areas. They play out in environments that are bandwidth-constrained, intermittently connected, and operationally unforgiving. 

The role is deeply hands-on, but it expects you to shape what we build and how we build it, not just deliver what's specified.

What you'll do

Wir suchen eine:n SDR für unser Growth Team an unserem Standort in Berlin oder Hamburg. Werde Teil unseres Teams und baue mit uns das größte KI-gestützte FinTech für das Gesundheitswesen auf!
Das Level für diese Rolle legen wir gemeinsam im Prozess fest – abhängig von deiner Erfahrung und wie du im Interview überzeugst.
 
Über Nelly
Wir bauen das AI-Driven Financial Operating System für das europäische Gesundheitswesen und lösen so die größten Herausforderungen für Patient:innen und Praxen. Damit schaffen wir, was keine Bank oder Softwareplattform bewältigen kann. Unsere All-In-One Plattform verwandelt chaotische administrative Prozesse in intelligente, automatisierte Arbeitsabläufe, von der Patientenbetreuung über die Abrechnung bis hin zu Zahlungen der nächsten Generation. Denn wir sind davon überzeugt: Das Gesundheitswesen sollte weniger mit Papierkram und mehr mit Menschen zu tun haben.
Warum? Europa ist mit einem massiven Mangel an medizinischen Fachkräften konfrontiert. Wenn wir die Arbeitsweise von Praxen nicht überdenken, wird das System nicht mithalten können. Mit unserer Series B Finanzierung in Höhe von über 50 Millionen Euro von Weltklasse-Investoren setzen wir unsere Vision in die Tat um.
Was dich erwartet: Wir arbeiten mit dem besten Team und geben gemeinsam jeden Tag alles. Wir setzen auf Talent Density, weil außergewöhnliche Menschen alle um sie herum besser machen. Bei Nelly bewegen wir uns schnell und erwarten, dass alle mithalten. Stillstand ist keine Option, deshalb investieren wir stark in Weiterentwicklung.  KI ist bei uns kein Nice-to-have. Wir erwarten, dass du sie täglich nutzt und geben dir alle Möglichkeiten, dies zu tun. Du bekommst Vertrauen und Verantwortung, dafür erwarten wir, dass du Dinge ansprichst, auch wenn es unbequem ist.

Deine Rolle bei uns:
Du bist die erste Stimme, die potenzielle Nelly-Kund:innen von uns hören – und die Person, die entscheidet, welche Leads es bis zur Demo schaffen. Konkret heißt das:
Du baust dir deine eigene Pipeline auf: von der ersten Kontaktaufnahme bis zum gebuchten Demo-Termin, komplett eigenverantwortlich.

Du sprichst täglich mit ca. 60 potenziellen Kund:innen – am Telefon, per Cold Call und im Inbound-Gespräch – und entscheidest selbst, wie du sie überzeugst.

Du qualifizierst Leads sauber und ordnest sie korrekt bestehenden Accounts zu, damit im Vertriebsteam niemand bei null anfängt.

Du gibst Marketing direktes Feedback zur Lead-Qualität – deine Beobachtungen fließen sofort in die nächste Kampagne ein.

Du bist Teil von Messen und Events und bekommst dadurch Einblick, wie Nelly bei echten Kund:innen ankommt – nicht nur am Telefon.

Du arbeitest eng mit Partnerships und Marketing zusammen und siehst, wie dein Beitrag den gesamten Sales-Zyklus verkürzt

Das bringst du mit:
Du hast Hunter-Mentalität und Can-do-Attitude – Telefonieren und Überzeugen ist für dich kein notwendiges Übel, sondern macht dir Spaß.

Du übernimmst Ownership über deine eigene Pipeline, ohne dass dir jemand hinterherlaufen muss.

Du bist stressresistent und KPI-getrieben – Zahlen motivieren dich, sie schüchtern dich nicht ein.

Du kommunizierst klar und überzeugend 

Du sprichst Deutsch auf C2-Niveau

Diese Rolle ist nichts für dich, wenn:
Du lieber in Ruhe an einer Sache feilst, statt täglich viele Calls zu führen und dich an klaren Zahlen messen zu lassen.

Dich Ablehnung am Telefon frustriert statt anzuspornen – Cold Calling gehört zum Alltag, nicht zur Ausnahme.

Du einen klar vorgezeichneten, unveränderlichen Prozess erwartest – der Inbound/Outbound-Split verschiebt sich je nach Lead-Lage, und du musst dich flexibel darauf einstellen.

Unser Interviewprozess:
First Call mit deiner TA Partnerin (online, 30 Minuten) 

Second Call mit deinem potenziellen Team Lead (online, ca. 45 Minuten) 

On Site Gespräch, ca 60 Minuten

BVG-Ticket oder Swapfiets-Mitgliedschaft, damit du schnell unterwegs bist

Urban Sports Club-Mitgliedschaft, damit Bewegung und Ausgleich nicht zu kurz kommen

500€ L&D Budget, um dich weiterzuentwickeln

28 Urlaubstage, steigend, bis 30 Tage erreicht sind

Flexible Arbeitszeiten und ein Hybrid-Setup

Bis zu 4 Wochen Workation

Ein hundefreundliches Büro mit guter Atmosphäre und einem Team mit dem es Spaß macht zu arbeiten

Snacks und ein Kühlschrank voller kalter Getränke

Knowledge sharing

7+ years of hands-on software engineering experience, ideally building complex products in dynamic environments
Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Computer Science or a related discipline
Deep proficiency in TypeScript, including advanced type-level programming

Hands-on experience with cloud platforms such as Google Cloud, and the services that typically come with them.
You embrace AI tools in your workflow and are driven to master emerging technologies
You champion code quality and drive best practices across the team
You thrive in fast-moving environments - seeking opportunities to learn, grow, and both give and receive feedback
Strong English skills (C1 or better); German is a plus but not required

GraphQL
Node.js & Prisma (ORM)
Python & FastAPI & SQLAlchemy
Postgres for storage & Redis for caching & messages
Terraform / Open Tofu orchestrating Google Cloud Platform

jobs.title: IT-Spezialist:in Software- & Platform-Engineering (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Die Albert Schweitzer Stiftung für unsere Mitwelt suchtIT-Spezialist:in Software- & Platform-Engineering (m/w/d)
zum nächstmöglichen Termin in Berlin (hoher Homeoffice-Anteil möglich) mit 35 Wochenstunden (Vollzeit) in Festanstellung.

Unsere Vision ist eine Welt, in der kein Tier mehr für die Herstellung von Lebensmitteln leidet. Unsere Mission lautet: Gemeinsam Tierschutzstandards erhöhen und den Verbrauch von Tierprodukten senken. Mit unserer Arbeit wirken wir in den Bereichen Wirtschaft, Recht und Politik. Auf allen Ebenen gehen wir mit den jeweiligen Akteur:innen praktikable Schritte in Richtung eines respektvollen Umgangs mit den Tieren und erleichtern auch vermeintlichen Gegner:innen den Ausstieg aus bisherigen Handlungsmustern.

Als IT-Spezialist:in Software- & Platform-Engineering wirst du Teil unseres bislang zweiköpfigen IT-Teams, das mit einem reibungslosen, effizienten und sicheren Betrieb von IT-Infrastruktur und Online-Auftritten dafür sorgt, dass unsere Arbeit ihre maximale Wirkung entfalten kann.  

Das bewirkst du bei unsDu legst das technische Fundament, auf dem die gesamte Arbeit der Albert Schweitzer Stiftung für unsere Mitwelt aufbaut, und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Systeme zuverlässig, sicher und zukunftsfähig bleiben.
Als IT-Spezialist:in Software- & Platform-Engineering bist du verantwortlich für die Konzeption, Planung und Umsetzung der Weiterentwicklung unserer IT-Infrastruktur und -Anwendungslandschaft: Du betreust unsere Hosting-Infrastruktur in der Cloud und entwickelst sie kontinuierlich weiter, sorgst dafür, dass zentrale Systeme wie CRM, Spendenplattform, Webseiten, Kampagnen und Mailing-Infrastruktur reibungslos miteinander Daten austauschen, und entwickelst dafür auch individuelle Softwarelösungen.

Im Einzelnen bedeutet dasDu betreust, entwickelst und integrierst sowohl unsere bestehenden als auch neu einzuführende IT-Systeme, wie auch unsere DevOps-Plattform, zum Beispiel GitHub und AWS, weiter. 

Du konzipierst, implementierst, dokumentierst und rollst neue IT-Projekte & Lösungen aus.

Du stehst im engen Austausch mit Kolleg:innen im IT-Team und in anderen Fachbereichen und berätst zu fachlichen wie nicht-fachlichen Anforderungen, etwa IT-Sicherheit oder Usability.

Du unterstützt und berätst die Fachbereiche bei der Konzeption und Implementierung von IT-Lösungen – von der Einschätzung technischer Machbarkeit und Aufwand über die technische Umsetzung bis hin zur Auswahl geeigneter Off-the-Shelf-Komponenten.

Dein ProfilDu hast mindestens fünf Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung sowie im Betrieb moderner Anwendungs- und Plattform-Infrastrukturen (z. B. Cloud/PaaS, CI/CD, Integrationen).

Im Bereich DevOps und IT-Infrastruktur bringst du herausragende Erfahrung mit.

Du verfügst über sehr gute Kenntnisse in Softwareentwicklung (vorzugsweise PHP/Laravel) und der Integration von Anwendungen per REST oder GraphQL APIs

Für die Entwicklung von Web-Anwendungen beherrschst du HTML, (S)CSS und Javascript/Typescript und hast auch Erfahrung in der Anpassung von PHP-basierten CMS-Systemen wie Kirby und Statamic.

Du bist in der Lage, ein IT-Projekt von Anfang bis Ende zu planen, durchzuführen und zu Ende zu bringen.

Dabei arbeitest du zusammen mit fachlichen Stakeholdern, von der Anforderungsanalyse über iterative Checkpoints bis zum Rollout .

Du nutzt KI-Systeme, um deine eigene Arbeit zu unterstützen, und kannst anderen dabei helfen, KI für ihre Ziele sinnvoll einzusetzen.

Gute Kenntnisse in der Automatisierung von Arbeitsabläufen sind gefragt, mit KI-Tooling, Low-Code/No-Code-Plattformen oder klassisch per Scripting. 

Du hast gute Kenntnisse in IT-Sicherheit und Datenschutz.

Du kennst dich aus im Bereich Identitätsmanagement (IAM) per OAuth oder SAML.

Du bist team- und kommunikationsfähig und arbeitest serviceorientiert sowie selbständig.

Mit deiner herausragenden Problemlösungskompetenz gehst du auch komplexe technische Herausforderungen sicher an.

Auch wenn es mal stressig wird, weil z. B. eine Deadline näher rückt, bleibst du konzentriert.

Deutsch und Englisch sprichst du verhandlungssicher (C1-Niveau).

Du arbeitest gerne mit anderen zusammen – auch wenn nicht alle an einem Ort sind.

Du identifizierst dich mit unserer Vision, Mission und Kultur.

Was wir dir bietenEine unbefristete Vollzeit-Stelle auf 35-Basis: Als Teil des IT-Teams bewirkst du direkt gesellschaftliche Veränderungen und verbesserst den Tierschutz.

Home-Office-Möglichkeiten: Du wohnst in Berlin oder Umgebung und arbeitest mit flexiblen, familienfreundlichen Arbeitszeiten im hybriden Modell (Homeoffice & Büro).

Professionelles Team: Kollegialer, offener Austausch in einem motivierten Team 

Hundefreundliche Büros inkl. „hundefreie“ Bereiche für Allergiker:innen sowie ergonomische Arbeitsplätze

Attraktive Vergütung: Unbefristet, Jahresgehalt zwischen 48.940,20 und 59.243,40 Euro (erfahrungsbasiert) + Bonuszahlungen 

Benefits: Cafeteria-Modell (finanzielle Vorteile, Deutschlandticket oder zusätzliche Urlaubstage), Zuschüsse zu Gesundheitsleistungen (z. B. B12 + D Bluttests) und betriebliche Altersvorsorge

Weiterbildung: Aktive Förderung von Fort- und Weiterbildungen

Haben wir dein Interesse geweckt?Dann schick uns deine Bewerbung bis zum 31.10.2026 per Bewerbungsbutton. Wir möchten von dir erfahren, was dich motiviert, bei der Albert Schweitzer Stiftung zu arbeiten, weshalb du die beste Person für diese Rolle bist und wann du bei uns anfangen könntest. 

Solltest du nicht alle Kriterien erfüllen, ermutigen wir dich trotzdem, dich zu bewerben - wir sind auf der Suche nach einer lernfähigen und motivierten Person, die in unser Team passt.
Wir sind überzeugt, dass vielfältige Perspektiven Entscheidungen verbessern können und begrüßen daher ausdrücklich Bewerbungen von Menschen verschiedener Hintergründe.

Bei Fragen zu der Stelle melde dich gerne bei Marie Mittermeier an .

jobs.description:
At Stark, we forge the future of European and national security through cutting-edge, AI-driven technology and unmatched engineering precision. As a premier defence technology company, our mission is clear: to equip NATO Allies and their partners  with next-generation autonomous defence platforms and advanced AI-driven software built to perform in the world’s most demanding environments.

We believe that true security stems from relentless innovation. By combining elite engineering talent with agile technology and an AI-native operational culture, Stark turns complex defence challenges into field-tested, multi-domain solutions.

Why Join Us?

The software and systems you work on directly protect personnel and defend European and national sovereignty.

You will work alongside industry-leading minds on autonomous systems, advanced propulsion, and secure cyber platforms.

We foster a fast-paced, collaborative environment where bold ideas are supported by serious R&D backing.

About the Team

Minerva Frontline is STARK's command and control software — the brain that connects operators to autonomous systems across multiple domains in real time. The Frontline team is based across Europe & the UK, working with our hardware teams to build mission-critical C2 capabilities for use in active operational environments.

We move fast, ship real software, and operate under constraints most engineers never encounter — low-bandwidth networks, air-gapped devices, high-stakes decision loops. We are a tight-knit team of zero-ego, mission-driven developers. There is no room for abstraction for its own sake. Everything we build ends up in the hands of real operators in the field.

If you want to build software which will make a tangible difference to the security of Europe, we want to hear from you.

Your Mission

STARK is looking for a Senior Software Engineer (Frontend Systems) to expand our mission management software. We are not looking for someone who just works on Jira tickets. We need a frontend systems thinker who balances rapid delivery with the deep system understanding required to answer: 'What is the right solution for the overall system, and what is the frontend's role in it?'

You will build and evolve the frontend as a robust, high-performance architecture. You have the high-agency to navigate the physical constraints of our hardware, challenge the backend with hard questions, and translate complex data streams into a clear, calm UI for operators under extreme cognitive load. While you actively provide impulses for our overall system evolution, your core focus remains hands-on engineering.

We consistently rely on agentic AI workflows. While these agents accelerate development, they also introduce entirely new classes of technical challenges. Your role is to set strict architectural guardrails, rigorously orchestrate these agents, and collaborate with the team to solve the novel integration and quality problems that arise in this new engineering paradigm.

Responsibilities

System Thinking through the Frontend Lens: You don't need to write path-planning algorithms, but you must understand how they constrain the UI. You engineer highly optimized frontend solutions that handle high-frequency telemetry and asynchronous data streams while strictly minimizing computational load to preserve critical battery life on field devices.

Mission-Critical UI & UX: You translate complex data into immediate situational awareness. You understand UX as cognitive load management for operators under stress. You implement interfaces that are deterministic, error-tolerant, and relentlessly focused on providing clarity out of chaos.

Strategic Sparring Partner: You align rapid delivery with long-term system health. Instead of just accepting what the backend provides, you proactively challenge APIs and data structures if they threaten frontend performance or the operator's experience.

Mastering Agentic Workflows: You don't just prompt; you engineer alongside AI. You set strict architectural guardrails, rigorously validate outputs, and proactively solve the novel integration and quality challenges that arise in this new paradigm.

Engineering for Extreme Constraints: Build high-performance, framework-less user interfaces (Vanilla TS, Web Components) that function flawlessly under extreme real-world conditions (low bandwidth, air-gapped networks).

Collaborative Excellence: You are a team multiplier. You raise the level of the entire team by sharing knowledge, providing valuable impulses for our system design, and facilitating open, fact-based discussions with zero ego.

Required Skills

System-Level Frontend Seniority: Deep, practical expertise in Vanilla TypeScript/JavaScript and the native web platform (DOM API, Event Loop, Memory Management). You view the frontend not as a collection of pages, but as a complex, stateful system interacting with the physical world.

Constraint-Driven Engineering: The ability to engineer solutions that anticipate and mitigate hardware realities—specifically managing latency, handling data bursts, and optimizing for constrained compute and battery life.

AI-Engineering Competence: Practical experience integrating agent-based coding tools into your workflow. You understand how to structure architecture for AI, rigorously validate its output, and solve the novel integration challenges these tools create.

Mission-Oriented Execution: You balance the drive for rapid delivery with a critical mindset. You proactively question requirements and always evaluate technical decisions from the operator's perspective on the ground.

Strong Team Player & Zero-Ego: You have the maturity to moderate technical decisions, compromise, and always put the mission above your own ego.

Mobility: Ability to travel as needed.

Nice-To-Have

Practical experience building comprehensive design systems (ideally using native Web Components).

Experience with real-time data streaming architectures (WebSockets, WebRTC) or handling high-frequency telemetry.

Experience in geographic mapping, GIS, or complex Canvas/WebGL rendering in the browser.

Experience working with unmanned systems, ideally in command-and-control, mission management, or operator-facing software.

From there you build outward to 2028: a global organisation with local units in the UK, Ukraine, and Greece, each running common STARK processes under its own national authority. Organisation & leadership

Own the full flight test organisation across four pillars: Pilots & Operators, Flight Test Engineering, Flight Test Operations, and Safety & Compliance.

Hire and develop the pillar leads, and build the career ladders and competency standards that take the German organisation to its ~40+-person target and beyond.

Carry budget, headcount, schedule, and tempo accountability for flight test as a whole.

Define STARK’s flight test strategy across all platforms (Virtus, Cascade, Gambit and the small to large scale effectors that follow).

Own the envelope-expansion and build-up philosophy: how a test point moves from simulation to flying testbed (for example a Twin Otter-class surrogate) to the air vehicle, de-risking at each step.

Own the master Flight Test Operations Manual (FTOM), the test-planning methodology (test cards, Flight and Test Readiness Reviews), and the flight test engineering (FTE) and instrumentation (FTI) standards.

Own the data lifecycle: quality, traceability, and results that stand up as cerification evidence.

Flight safety & airworthiness

Hold the independent flight test safety function: Safety Review Boards, hazard analysis, risk acceptance, abort criteria, and emergency response at every test site.

Keep flight test activity inside approved limits (Permit-to-Fly, operational authorisations) and drive STARK toward its LUC and DOA-grade airworthiness posture.

Give safety dissent a hard, codified path to the Accountable Manager that schedule pressure cannot override.

Campaign delivery

Deliver three campaign types through the Operations pillar: production-acceptance flights at volume, developmental flight tests  for engineering, and customer-facing demonstration and qualification  flights.

Stand up a high-throughput production-acceptance regime as delivery contracts convert to volume, and run it as its own discipline, in parallel to the engineering flight tests.

jobs.description:
Job description

Team & Reporting Line: 

Our Mission 

At constellr, we use thermal intelligence from space to understand what is happening on Earth - where, when and at scale. Our satellite constellation delivers high-resolution land surface temperature data, giving governments, defence organisations, commercial operators and global institutions the intelligence they need to monitor change, assess risk and make better-informed decisions.

From national security and critical infrastructure to agriculture and climate resilience, constellr turns temperature into actionable intelligence for a changing world.

Your Role

As our Senior Business Development Manager for the Public Sector, you will join the Commercial team and lead constellr’s growth with civil government customers – environmental ministries, national and regional agencies, and European institutions – who need reliable, decision-grade thermal intelligence to manage water, agriculture, infrastructure and climate resilience. 

This is not a data-reselling role. You will sell data intelligence and analytics: understanding what public bodies are trying to achieve, shaping how our land surface temperature products and insights fit their mandates, and guiding them through funding cycles and formal procurement. You will work closely with our Product, Earth observation science and Solutions teams to translate remote sensing capability into solutions that answer real governmental needs, and alongside colleagues covering commercial, industrial and defence markets to build a coherent go-to-market across the business. 

You will own a strategic portfolio from first conversation to signed contract, including major upcoming national and EU tenders, and build on constellr’s existing success in European programmes such as Copernicus. With the launch of the world’s first commercial thermal infrared constellation, the relationships you build and the deals you win will define how governments use thermal data for years to come. 

Key responsibilities

Public-Sector Growth: Own and grow constellr’s civil public-sector business, developing a targeted pipeline across environmental ministries, national agencies, research-funded programmes and European institutions. 

Selling Data Intelligence: Lead value-based sales of thermal data, analytics and insight services, positioning solutions around customer outcomes rather than raw imagery. 

Tenders & Procurement: Identify, qualify and lead responses to public tenders and framework calls, working with procurement and tender teams and coordinating internal bid teams through to submission and negotiation. 

Funding Cycles & Programmes: Map national, EU and ESA funding cycles, programmes and budget timelines, and shape opportunities early so constellr is positioned well ahead of formal procurement. 

Proposal Management: Lead proposals for funded programmes, framework contracts and consortium bids – from opportunity strategy and partner selection through to compelling, compliant submissions. 

Stakeholder Engagement: Build trusted, senior relationships with decision-makers, technical users and procurement officers, speaking credibly to each audience. 

Science-to-Market: Act as the bridge between science and customers – partner with our scientists and product teams to translate remote sensing capabilities into clear use cases, pilots and solution proposals that meet governmental requirements. 

Commercial Leadership: Hold your ground in complex negotiations, protect deal value and represent constellr confidently in front of senior public officials. 

Partnerships & Ecosystem: Develop relationships with research institutes, system integrators and geospatial partners to access and win larger public programmes. 

Market Intelligence: Feed customer and market insight back into product, pricing and commercial strategy, and represent constellr at key conferences and public-sector events. 

Forecasting & Reporting: Maintain an accurate pipeline and forecast in our CRM and deliver against agreed commercial targets. 

Job requirements

About you 

Required: 

Significant (typically 8+ years) experience in business development or sales of geospatial, Earth observation or data analytics solutions, with a strong track record selling to civil public-sector customers. 

Proven experience winning public tenders and navigating government procurement, funding cycles and budget processes. 

A solid understanding of remote sensing and how satellite-derived data and analytics are used to meet governmental needs. 

An advanced degree (MSc or PhD) in physics, geoscience, remote sensing or a related STEM field – or equivalent experience – giving you credibility with technical and scientific stakeholders. 

Strong proposal and bid management experience, ideally including EU, ESA or nationally funded programmes and consortium bids. 

Experience selling data intelligence, analytics or information services rather than hardware or raw data alone. 

The ability to bridge science and industry, with a senior, confident presence – able to stand your ground in negotiations and build credibility with ministry-level stakeholders. 

An established network across European public-sector, research or geospatial communities. 

Excellent communication skills in English and German. 

Willingness to travel regularly for customer meetings, public-sector events and industry conferences. 

Nice to Have: 

Experience selling into defence, security or dual-use programmes. 

A background in an applied research institute, geoscience or remote sensing environment. 

Exposure to security research, resilience or critical infrastructure programmes. 

Familiarity with European programmes such as Copernicus, ESA or EU-funded research and innovation calls. 

Experience in technology transfer, innovation management or strategic roles within public-sector or research organisations. 

Additional European languages, particularly French. 

Experience in a fast-growing New Space or scale-up company. 

Why join constellr?

High-Impact National Security Mission: Be part of an ambitious mission to launch the world’s first commercial thermal infrared constellation, delivering sovereign-grade "behavioural" intelligence from space to close critical blind spots for defence, intelligence, and maritime surveillance agencies.

Fast-Paced "New Space" Innovation: Work at the leading edge of a rapidly evolving defence sector. By leveraging modern, agile New Space methodologies, you will help design, build, and deploy dual-use thermal payloads into operational orbit at a speed and scale that traditional aerospace models simply cannot match.

Broad Interdisciplinary Exposure: Accelerate your professional growth by collaborating daily with a diverse, international cohort of astrophysicists, software developers, and defence-system engineers.

Inclusive & Scientific Culture: Join a high-trust team deeply committed to diversity, inclusion, and scientific excellence, where academic curiosity is paired with high autonomy and a flat hierarchy.

Financial Upside & Well-being: Benefit from a Virtual Share Option Plan (VSOP) for permanent employees, giving you a true stake in the company's growth, alongside highly flexible hybrid working models.

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Staff Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you help developers find and fix security issues. Those issues live in the code they write, and you set the technical direction for the static analysis engine that finds them.

Your work spans two complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the engine side, you shape how the static analysis toolkit models a program: parsing source into intermediate representations, resolving symbols, building call graphs, and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You define the architecture and specifications the team builds against, and you delegate component specifications within them to engineers and to the AI agents that implement them. On the evaluation side, you build and apply tooling that tests, measures, and validates what the engine finds against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities.

What the engine can model and how we measure what it finds are parts of one picture. As a Staff engineer you hold that picture, shape the long-range technical goals of the team, and raise the bar for every engineer on it. We build the engine with AI agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. We expect you to direct that work effectively and with good judgment, and to help the team do the same.

What you do

Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for the team's highest-scope initiatives from design through delivery, shipping large features with minimal guidance and shaping the long-range goals of the team

Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review

Set the technical direction for the AI-assisted tooling that implements, reviews, and validates engine changes and findings, design the checks that decide whether an agent-written change or generated result is fit to merge, and measure detection quality against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. That includes static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to CWE and OWASP, and the test fixtures that prove they work.

Own the architecture of the program model (parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis) and of the pipeline that turns source code into findings, and define how both extend to new languages and frameworks

Solve technical problems of the highest scope and complexity, actively seek out difficult impediments affecting the whole team, and advocate for improvements to quality, security, and performance with Product Management, UX, and partner teams such as Code Security and Composition Analysis

Mentor all engineers on the team through code review and pairing, remove blockers to their autonomy, and shepherd the definition and improvement of our internal standards through review

Participate in on-call rotations to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues

Define the overarching architecture and specification documents for the engine, delegate component specifications within them, and drive their implementation by AI agents and engineers working independently through phased plans, small reviewable units of change, and specifications kept in lockstep with the code

Build and maintain the harness, agent instructions, and agentic skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy, including separate coding and reviewing agents, rules and tests the coding agents cannot change, independent review panels of agents from different model providers, and performance, API, and dependency gates, with risky changes escalated to human review

Stay current with research in program analysis and security, run AI-assisted research and spikes, and turn the findings into prototypes, proposals, and upstream contributions, including responsible disclosure of findings in open source projects

What you bring

Experience building your own LLM tooling, such as a harness, an agent pipeline, or evaluations, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't

Extensive professional experience writing, testing, and reviewing production code in Rust, Go, or a comparable systems language, with depth in at least one. The engine is Rust, the analyzer wrapper is Go, and the monolith integration is Ruby, and we value willingness to work across them.

Experience with performance optimization and with containerized workflows and CI/CD (we use Docker heavily)

A deep program analysis and static analysis background, such as parsing and ASTs, intermediate representations (SSA, control-flow and call graphs), taint and data-flow analysis, type inference, incremental and fixpoint computation, or writing detection rules, with the ability to read, evaluate, and apply the research literature

Deep application security experience, such as vulnerability research, secure code review, or writing detection rules, and fluency with vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10, CWE)

Demonstrated capacity to communicate clearly and concisely about complex technical, architectural, and organizational problems, and to write architecture and design specifications that bring a team to a decision

A track record of taking ownership of ambiguous, team-wide problems and shipping them from concept to production with minimal guidance, with specific, regular async updates on progress, blockers, risks, and next steps

Experience defining a system's overarching architecture, delegating component specifications to engineers and AI agents, and getting them implemented reliably

A track record of mentoring engineers, raising a team's technical bar, and influencing technical direction by achieving consensus with peers and leadership

Helpful experience

Familiarity with popular web or mobile application frameworks and how they handle input, data, and configuration

Experience designing guardrails for agent-written code, such as mutation testing, fuzzing, and CI gates the coding agent cannot modify

A record of engaging with the research community, such as publications, tool papers, or upstream open source contributions in program analysis or security

About the team

The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories.

We work closely with the Code Security team on scanning rules & flows, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec Section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.

We’re on a mission to make migration easy.

We started building Marshmallow in 2017. Since then, we’ve grown from 3 to 700+ people, gained unicorn status, raised ~£140M over three funding rounds, turned profitable, insured millions of drivers and lent millions in car loans.

But we’re only just getting started. Our goal is to become one of the largest financial services providers in the world. Over the next 10 years we’ll grow exponentially, not only by scaling our existing products, but also by building new ones.

We’ve created an environment where curious, tenacious people win and grow together. If that sounds motivating, this could be the place for you.

London (hybrid, 3 days in office)
 
Car Finance at Marshmallow
Marshmallow is opening up access to credit to migrants, bringing a brand new product to market which provides newcomers to the UK with fairly priced car finance for the first time.
Our Car Finance team is building a new generation lending platform from the ground up, making it simple, transparent and accessible for people who need finance to get on the road. We work closely with dealers, brokers and customers to make sure that every application, decision and interaction is fast, fair and easy to understand.
Because we’re a small, high-performing team, everyone has real ownership. We combine hands-on operations with a strong focus on automation and technology. We’re designing highly automated, AI-powered processes that let us move faster and smarter than traditional lenders.

The Role
We're hiring a Data Scientist to sit at the heart of how we lend: who we say yes to, at what price, and how we know it's working.
Our customers are people that traditional lenders struggle to assess. Many are new to the UK, have thin or no credit files, and don't fit neatly into off-the-shelf bureau scores. That makes credit decisioning at Marshmallow a genuinely hard, genuinely interesting problem: we combine bureau data, Open Banking, insurance, application and behavioural data to build a view of risk that others can't, and we need to do it in a way that is fair, explainable and compliant.
This role sits between a traditional credit analyst and a data scientist. You'll build and monitor scorecards, design and test credit strategies, dig into portfolio performance to find out what's really going on, and turn large, messy datasets into insights that change how we lend. You'll own your work end-to-end: from framing the question and pulling the data through to modelling, presenting a recommendation and seeing it live in our decision engine.
You'll be working with a small team and a modern stack, alongside a Head of Credit who has built this function from scratch and who will give you real ownership from day one. This is not a role where you hand models over a wall and move on - you'll see the impact of your decisions immediately.
 
What you'll be doing
Build, validate and monitor application and behavioural scorecards, using bureau, Open Banking and internal data to improve how we assess new-to-UK and thin-file customers.

Design, test and refine our credit strategy: cut-offs, affordability rules, pricing tiers and limits, with a clear view of the trade-off between risk, volume and margin.

Run experiments and champion/challenge tests to prove that changes to policy and models actually work before we scale them.

Explore new data sources and alternative signals, and build the case for using (or not using) them in decisioning.

Support model governance: document what you build, evidence that it treats customers fairly, and help us meet our Consumer Duty, CONC and model risk obligations.

Work with our engineers to get models and rules into production, and use AI tooling to make yourself and the team faster.

What You'll Bring
Must have
2–5 years' experience in decision science or data science within consumer lending or another regulated financial services environment.

Hands-on experience developing or materially refining credit scorecards or risk models (logistic regression and/or gradient boosting), including the practicalities: sample design, binning, reject inference, validation and monitoring.

Experience working with Open Banking or other alternative data in credit decisioning.

SQL user, and comfortable working with large, imperfect datasets.

A solid grounding in statistics and a good instinct for when a result is real and when it isn't.

Commercial judgement: you can translate a model output into a lending decision and explain the trade-offs to a non-technical audience.

Curiosity and ownership. You ask why, you dig until you find the answer, and you'd rather ship something and improve it than wait for perfection.

Nice to have
Motor finance or other secured lending experience.

Experience of working within a rapidly scaling lending environment.

Familiarity with UK consumer credit regulation and how it shapes model design and use.

Experience using LLMs to speed up analytical work.

You already know some of the tooling Marshmallow uses: Snowflake, Python, Claude, Linear, Notion

Private medical insurance with Vitality, mental health support with Oliva

Personal learning budget and 2 dedicated L&D days a year

Monthly flexible benefits budget to spend as you choose

25 days holiday plus bank holidays

About us:

About us:

BVNK is the stablecoin-powered financial stack for enterprises. We're now part of Mastercard, and together we're building a network for every form of money – one that delivers more reach, more capability and more choice.

We enable businesses to build financial products, unlock new markets, and move money in seconds across 130+ countries, with 40+ licenses for fiat and digital assets globally. Processing billions annually, we empower enterprises worldwide to send, receive, convert, and settle stablecoins and fiat seamlessly through a single integration.

Our mission is to accelerate global money movement, and we're assembling a world-class team to make it happen.

Trusted by industry leaders like Corpay, Worldpay, Deel, and Flywire, we deliver the infrastructure that makes new forms of money usable within the financial systems customers already rely on today.

By combining Mastercard's global payment reach and trusted networks with BVNK's stablecoin infrastructure, we're building the trusted operating layer for the evolution of money movement, helping customers participate in emerging digital networks without having to rebuild their businesses around every new innovation.

We're a diverse team spread across EMEA, North America, and APAC, with a shared belief that stablecoins are the new infrastructure layer for financial services, and that BVNK is at the forefront of this shift.

We're incredibly honored to have been recognized by:

CNBC World's Top Fintech Companies (2026)

FXC Intelligence Top 100 Cross-border Payment Companies (2026)

Newsweek's The Top 100 Global Most Loved Workplaces (three years running, most recently 2025)

LinkedIn as one of the Top 20 Startups in the UK (2025)

About this role in the team:

We're looking for a Product Manager to own the product vision, strategy, and delivery for the Reporting & Customer Reconciliation subdomain within BVNK's Ledger domain. You'll  work closely with engineering, design, finance, operations, and commercial teams to define how BVNK's customers  and BVNK's own internal teams — see, understand, and trust their financial data.

The Ledger domain is the financial backbone of BVNK, a single, trusted source of truth for all customer and transactional balances across products, currencies, and rails. Within this domain, the Reporting & Customer Reconciliation subdomain is responsible for providing clear, consistent financial views derived from the ledger for both internal and external reporting. Through the Reporting Service, Search Service, and downstream data surfaces,it ensures that positions, balances, and movements are accurately represented for Finance, Risk, Operations, and customers.

This is a high-impact, cross-functional role. As part of BVNK's Billing 2.0 vision and the drive toward a 100% self-serve customer experience, you'll define and deliver the product capabilities that give customers full transparency; enabling them to reconcile invoices, audit charges programmatically, and automate close processes, while also building the internal reporting foundations that Finance, Reconciliation, and Operations depend on to scale.

Key Areas of Responsibilities:

Own the product vision and roadmap for Reporting & Customer Reconciliation — Define the strategy for how BVNK exposes financial data to customers and internal teams, aligning with the broader Ledger domain mission and company objectives (Billing 2.0, self-serve experience, MiCA compliance).

Drive transaction report fee breakdowns — Define requirements and work with engineering to ensure transaction reports and APIs properly include both real-time and invoiced fees, broken down by fee type

Build the customer reconciliation product — Define and deliver customer-facing reconciliation endpoints and reporting surfaces that enable enterprise clients to programmatically audit charges, automate close processes, and reconcile against invoices.

Improve internal financial reporting — Partner with Finance, Reconciliation, and Operations to understand their data needs and deliver standardised reports and views that replace fragmented, manual processes with reliable, automated data pipelines.

Collaborate across domains — Work with the Billing & Fees, Wallets, Balances , Digital Assets, Treasury, and Reconciliation domain to ensure reporting data is consistent and accurate end-to-end.

Define reporting for multi-entity and regulatory requirements — As BVNK expands across jurisdictions and customer types, ensure reporting structures correctly represent entity-specific data, segregation requirements, and regulatory obligations (MiCA safekeeping, EMI reconciliation).

Own stakeholder relationships — Serve as the primary product contact for Reporting & Customer Reconciliation. Engage regularly with Commercial (AMs/CSMs), Finance, Operations, and enterprise customers to gather requirements, validate solutions, and communicate roadmap priorities.

Measure and iterate — Define and track KPIs for reporting accuracy, customer adoption of reconciliation tools, reduction in manual reconciliation effort, and internal stakeholder satisfaction. Use data to inform roadmap prioritisation and demonstrate impact.

Ship with quality — Write clear PRDs, user stories, and acceptance criteria. Participate in architecture reviews and technical design submissions. Run beta programmes with select customers and internal teams to validate reporting capabilities before general availability.

What we need from you: 

5+ years of product management experience in fintech, payments, or financial services — ideally with exposure to ledger systems, financial reporting, or reconciliation products.

Deep understanding of financial data and reporting — you've worked with transaction data, balance reporting, reconciliation workflows, or invoicing systems. You understand concepts like double-entry bookkeeping, ledger postings, balance snapshots, and fee structures or can learn them quickly.

Experience building internal and customer-facing data products — you've defined and delivered reporting APIs, dashboards, data exports, or reconciliation tools that serve both external customers and internal operations teams.

Strong cross-functional collaboration skills — you're comfortable working with engineering, finance, operations, compliance, and commercial teams. You can translate complex financial requirements into clear product specifications and negotiate priorities across stakeholders with competing needs.

Data-driven decision making — you use quantitative and qualitative data to inform roadmap decisions, measure product impact, and communicate outcomes to leadership.

Technical fluency — you don't need to write code, but you can engage meaningfully with engineers on API design, data models, event-driven architectures, and database schemas. You're comfortable with tools like Snowflake, QuickSight, or similar BI/data warehousing platforms.

Experience in a fast-paced, scaling environment — you've operated in a startup or scale-up where scope is broad, resources are constrained, and you need to make pragmatic trade-offs between ideal and achievable.

Excellent written and verbal communication — you write clear PRDs, run effective stakeholder meetings, and can present product strategy to senior leadership with confidence.

Remote-first mindset — you're effectively working across time zones in an asynchronous-first culture, using Slack, Confluence, and Jira as primary collaboration tools.

Nice to have:

Experience with regulated financial services (EMI, VASP) and compliance reporting requirements (MiCA, safeguarding, client money rules).

Background in B2B payments platforms, stablecoin infrastructure, or crypto-adjacent products.

Familiarity with reconciliation platforms (Duco, Xero, or similar) and financial ledger systems.

Experience working with multi-tenant architectures and entity-level data segregation.

Understanding of event-driven data pipelines (Kafka, outbox patterns) and how they impact data consistency in reporting.

Product experience with self-serve billing or invoicing platforms.

What you can expect from us:

Fair and competitive salary at every stage of your growth

Flexible working hours, with hybrid working at its heart

A culture built on passionate, growth-minded people

A flexible approach to holiday

Opportunities to travel to our offices around the world

An open and creative environment where you can help us define the future of BVNK, its culture, and its opportunity sets

At BVNK, we are focused on building a diverse and inclusive team. While you may not meet all of our requirements, we’d encourage you to apply if you meet the majority of our expectations. You may be a great fit for this role or another role in our team.

This role is not programme responsible. Every Project Director is paired with a Lead Producer or Programme PM who owns the programme plan, budget and delivery. The Project Director is the creative and strategic counterpart to that delivery lead, and the two share accountability for the overall health of the project. In addition a technical director will be assigned, who is accountable for the proper design and delivery of the technical aspects of the programme. 

Key Responsibilities

The essential functions include, but are not limited to the following:

Vision, creative and quality

Oversees quality, technical and creative objectives, making sure client goals are met within the budget and schedule

Leads regular reviews, balancing client objectives with commercial reality.

Client strategy and stakeholder management

Owns the senior client relationship on strategy and quality 

Builds a working knowledge of the client's business and translates their goals into a project vision the team can build against. 

Leads senior stakeholder communication on creative and strategic matters, and is the escalation point when a client has concerns about the work itself. Commercial and scheduling escalations sit with the delivery lead

Technology

Can hold a credible conversation with engineering leads, and with the client, about technical trade-offs that affect the creative ambition.

Does not need to be hands-on. Needs enough fluency to make informed calls and to know when to bring in a technical lead.

Keeps current with creative technology and brings relevant developments into project and pitch thinking.

Working with delivery

Paired with a Lead Producer or Programme PM who owns the programme plan, budget, resourcing and margin. 

Also teamed with a Technical Director who owns the technical architecture, advises on approach and communicates back to the technical team on scope 

Contributes to scoping and estimating: shapes what is being proposed and its level of ambition so estimates reflect what will actually get built.

Business Development

Ensures they are managing and billing incremental work scope or making decisions to zero change order based on client relationship and value 

HR

Line management of project team members, indirect management of adjacent departments or disciplines as it relates to the project

Leads performance reviews 

Ensures continued professional development / training of staff in their team

Participates in the interview and selection process for all project team members alongside the Lead Producer 

Serve as a role model and mentor within the project and externally; participate in knowledge shares and actively improve process

Required

A track record of leading creative direction on complex digital projects, ideally including apps or product-style builds rather than campaign work alone.

Comfortable owning senior client relationships and presenting to exec-level stakeholders.

Demonstrable experience working with technical fluency relevant to this project: Digital Twins, CMS systems, Web Front and Web Backend.

Experience line managing and growing a team.

Communicates a clear sense of direction and purpose for the team, in person and in writing.

Clear experience adapting well to changing priorities.

Remaining up to date on industry trends and developments.

Contract Type: Fixed Term Contract - 12 Months 

Location : London

jobs.description:
Location: Westminster, London 

Salary: Competitive 

Reporting to: Executive Editor 

The Role

Reform UK is seeking an exceptional Data & Analytics Lead to build a best-in-class organisation-wide data and insight function from the party's Westminster headquarters. This is a broader opportunity than a conventional web or social analytics role: the successful candidate will help bring together disparate strands of performance, audience, membership, campaign and operational information into a coherent decision-making system.

The Data & Analytics Lead will establish the data stack, reporting definitions, access, dashboards and analytical rhythms that allow senior leaders and teams across Reform UK to see what is happening, understand why and act quickly. Digital channels will be an important part of the role, but the aim is to create a shared source of decision-ready insight across the organisation wherever useful data exists.

What you'll do

Build the organisation-wide data and insight function

Map the major data sources, owners, definitions, access rights, reporting rhythms and decision needs across Reform UK, identifying duplication, gaps and areas where information is currently fragmented.

Design and implement a practical data stack that can bring together appropriate information from digital channels, website, search, email, ReformGo, membership, campaigns and other organisational systems.

Establish clear definitions, baselines, targets and data-quality standards so senior leaders are not making decisions from conflicting numbers.

Create a roadmap that moves the organisation from isolated reports and manual extracts towards trusted, timely and increasingly automated decision support.

Key Responsibilities

Build dashboards that drive decisions

Create intuitive dashboards and scorecards for senior leadership and operational teams, focused on decisions rather than data for its own sake.

Develop role-appropriate views so executives can see the organisation-wide picture while teams can drill into the detail they need to manage performance day to day.

Connect output and activity to outcomes wherever attribution is reasonable, helping teams understand movement from attention to owned relationship, repeat behaviour, membership, participation or other useful actions.

Automate recurring reporting and data preparation where practical, reducing manual effort and increasing the frequency and reliability of insight.

Ensure dashboards show trends, targets and context rather than isolated totals that can easily mislead.

Turn raw data into insight and action

Produce concise, decision-ready analysis that explains what changed, why it matters, what is likely driving it and what the organisation should do next.

Identify where audiences, members or supporters stop progressing through journeys and work with relevant teams to test improvements.

Create a disciplined test-and-learn framework with hypotheses, success criteria and post-test analysis so the organisation learns systematically rather than anecdotally.

Use segmentation and cohort analysis to uncover meaningful patterns in behaviour.

Embed data-driven decision-making across Reform UK

Work with the Executive Editor, Director of Operations and other senior stakeholders to establish regular performance and insight reviews that lead to impactful decisions.

Support Website, Video, Social, Communications, Campaigns, Membership, Operations and other teams with practical analysis, helping each function understand its own performance in the wider system.

Challenge weak assumptions and vanity metrics constructively, distinguishing signal from noise and making clear where the evidence is incomplete or attribution is uncertain.

Train colleagues to understand the dashboards and core metrics so data literacy increases throughout the organisation rather than becoming dependent on one analyst.

Own governance, compliance and trust

Be the internal expert on data governance for the analytics function, ensuring work aligns with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act, ICO guidance and relevant organisational policies.

Work closely with the DPO and system owners on lawful basis, consent, minimisation, retention, access, pseudonymisation, URL/log hygiene and appropriate use of personal data.

Maintain clear data lineage, permissions and documentation so key metrics are reproducible and sensitive information is available only to those who genuinely need it.

Performance and Leadership:

Build alerting and monitoring for material changes, broken journeys, unusual movements or data-quality failures where rapid intervention is valuable.

Build trusted relationships with senior leaders, digital teams, campaigns, membership, operations, suppliers and technical partners so the data function is seen as an enabler rather than a reporting bottleneck.

Communicate complex analysis in clear, plain English, surface new ideas and be confident presenting findings to senior decision-makers.

Manage external analytics, BI, data or technology suppliers where required, ensuring integrations, costs and deliverables are properly controlled.

Maintain political awareness and discretion when working with sensitive organisational, membership or campaign data and understand that some insights will be operationally or reputationally sensitive.

THE PERSON

We are looking for a senior data and analytics expert who has built practical insight capability before and can turn fragmented information into a trusted system that improves decisions.

Essential experience and capabilities

A proven track record of establishing or materially improving a data, analytics, BI or insight operation in a complex organisation.

Strong experience integrating disparate data sources and designing a practical reporting architecture rather than relying on disconnected manual reports.

Demonstrable ability to build dashboards that colleagues actually use, with clear metrics, trends, context, drill-downs and decision relevance.

Excellent analytical judgement: able to distinguish signal from noise, explain uncertainty, avoid misleading attribution and turn numbers into actionable insight.

Strong technical competence with relevant data, analytics and BI tools, including the ability to work effectively with APIs, structured data, automation and modern dashboarding platforms.

Experience defining KPIs, baselines, targets, cohorts and measurement frameworks across multiple functions or stages of a user/member journey.

Outstanding communication skills, including the ability to explain complex analysis to non-technical senior stakeholders and influence decisions without hiding behind jargon.

Expert understanding of UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act, ICO guidance, consent, minimisation, retention, access controls and good data-governance practice.

Highly organised, self-sufficient and able to manage multiple stakeholders, systems, dependencies and priorities while maintaining clear documentation and data trust.

Proactive and pragmatic: willing to build a useful first version quickly, automate what matters and improve iteratively rather than waiting for a perfect enterprise architecture.

Strong interest in British politics and comfort handling sensitive information within a high-profile, mission-led political organisation where discretion and judgement are essential.

Willingness to work full-time from Reform UK's Westminster HQ and flex around major political, campaign and reporting moments when rapid analysis is required.

Highly desirable

Experience in political campaigning, media, membership organisations, subscriptions, CRM, advocacy or another environment where behaviour moves across multiple online and offline touchpoints.

Strong SQL, Python/R, data-modeling or warehouse experience and the ability to work directly with technical teams when deeper implementation is required.

Experience setting up experimentation, causal measurement, attribution or structured test-and-learn frameworks while communicating methodological limits clearly.

A track record of changing organisational behaviour through insight - for example reallocating resource, improving reach/conversion/retention, changing messaging or stopping low-value activity.

Why join Reform UK?

This is a rare opportunity to build the intelligence layer of a fast-growing national political organisation rather than inherit a narrow analytics brief. The successful candidate will bring fragmented information together and shape how senior leaders make decisions across Reform UK.

jobs.description:
Join AutogenAI – Revolutionising Bid and Proposal Writing 

At AutogenAI, we're changing how teams win work, not just how they write documents. Our platform is moving from AI that suggests to AI that acts: agents that research, draft and assemble proposals on a user's behalf, while the people who own the bid stay firmly in control. 

We're looking for a Principal Product Designer to shape that shift. You'll define how bid and proposal teams delegate to, supervise and trust AI, own the experience of key areas of our platform, and help raise the bar for design across the team.  

This is a hands-on individual contributor role: you'll do the work yourself, and your influence will reach well beyond your own features. 

You'll report to Chief Product Officer and join a design team of 4, working closely with Product, Engineering and Customer teams. 

This is a hybrid role (two days per week in our London office), 

What You’ll Do 

Shape product direction. Partner with Product and Engineering leads to frame the biggest user and business problems, influence the roadmap, and turn ambiguity into clear design strategy. 

Design how people work with agents. Move beyond "AI proposes, human accepts" to a calibrated range of autonomy, with clear moments for review, override and audit built in from the start. 

Make trust visible. Extend our trust patterns (source verification, calibrated confidence, visible progress) so every claim can be checked and every autonomous step traced back to what it did and why. 

Treat context as design material. Work with Engineering on what the system knows when it acts (instructions, memory, retrieved evidence, tool access) as part of the experience, alongside layout and flow. 

Own complex journeys end to end. Take multi-step, multi-user workflows from discovery to polished, production-ready UI, making the hard trade-offs and bringing stakeholders with you. 

Lead the design system's evolution. Keep agentic and AI-assisted patterns feeling like one coherent, accessible and refined product as we grow. 

Stay close to users. Lead research with customers and internal bid teams working under deadline and compliance pressure. Learn where they welcome AI autonomy and where they need control, and connect design decisions to measurable outcomes. 

Ship with care. Work with engineers on edge cases, failure states and QA so what we ship matches the design intent and stands up to enterprise and regulatory scrutiny. 

Help designers grow. Mentor, lead critiques, and shape how design is practised and valued at AutogenAI. 

What You’ll Bring 

Significant experience at Principal or strong Senior+ level designing B2B enterprise SaaS, with a track record of influencing direction beyond your own features. 

A portfolio showing clear problem framing, strategic thinking and high-quality UI for complex workflows: intricate processes, multiple user types or high-stakes decisions. 

Hands-on experience designing AI-powered products, ideally agentic ones. You know the difference between a system that suggests and one that acts, and what that shift asks of an interface. 

An understanding that trust and explainability live in system state and interaction sequencing, not only in microcopy or visual treatment. 

Working knowledge of accessibility standards (WCAG 2.2 AA) and inclusive design. 

The ability to lead through influence: clear communication, sound judgement on trade-offs, and confidence presenting to and challenging senior stakeholders. 

Comfort in a fast-moving environment, turning complex, AI-mediated work into simple, usable experiences. 

Expert use of Figma and modern prototyping practices, including AI-assisted design tools. 

Experience building or scaling a design system in a growing product organisation. 

Nice to Have 

Experience in regulated or compliance-heavy domains, such as public sector, healthcare or financial services. 

Familiarity with emerging agentic UX patterns and toolkits, such as AI SDK Elements. 

Experience with document editors, text-heavy tools or collaboration software. 

A background in bid or proposal workflows. 

Why Join Us 

Shape a category-defining product at the moment it moves from AI-assisted writing to autonomous, accountable proposal work. 

Work alongside a high-calibre, mission-driven team across Product, Engineering, Design, Sales and Customer Success. 

Real autonomy and ownership, and a genuine say in how design (and how AI acts on a user's behalf) is done here. 

Compensation and Benefits:   

Competitive Salary: c.£100,000 - £120,000 depending on experience. 

Stock Options: Meaningful equity in the company.  

Retirement Plan: Pension scheme to help secure your future.  

Paid Time Off: Unlimited vacation (Yes, you read right!)  

Flexible Work Options: This is a hybrid role (two days per week in our London office), 

Private Healthcare: Bupa Medical and Dental cover  

Life Insurance: Peace of mind for you and your family 

Paid parental leave: 16 weeks if you’ve just given birth, 4 weeks if your partner has just given birth (after one year of service)  

Values in Action: 

These aren’t just principles we print and forget – they’re how we work, how we treat each other, and how we deliver for our customers. They shape the company we are, and the one we aspire to become. 

Customers, Always: Everything starts with our customers. We walk in their shoes, speak their language, and build for their delight and success. We win when they win. 

Make It Happen: We move fast and take ownership. No waiting, no red tape – just action, urgency, and focus on outcomes. We ask for forgiveness, not permission.

jobs.title: Banking Accounting Manager
jobs.description:
🧡 About Alma

At Alma, we believe sustainable commerce depends on fair, well-balanced trade. Because finance plays a pivotal role in business, our mission is to put it back in its rightful place — serving merchants and consumers.

Our installment and deferred payment solutions help merchants boost sales by 20% or more, increase customer loyalty, and deliver a seamless shopping experience — without encouraging bad debt.

As the buy now pay later leader in France and active in 10 European countries, we've empowered over +25,000 merchants and 10 million consumers.

With 380+ Almakers and €100M+ ARR in 2025, Alma is scaling rapidly across Europe as a member of the Next40, and we're just getting started!

👐 About the team

Alma is a lender. We originate several million consumer receivables a year, carry them for a few weeks, and refinance them off a deliberately light balance sheet through securitization vehicles (Fonds Communs de Titrisation) and our other funding lines. We are regulated as a société de financement and a payment institution.

That changes what "accounting" means here. A lender's accounts are not a monthly deliverable produced at the end of a chain: they are the chain. Every payment event, every commission, every provision, every sale of receivables to an FCT has to become a journal entry that ties — to the transaction underneath it, to the general ledger above it, and to the prudential statements the regulator reads. At our scale and growth, this is a strategic topic, and one that is as much about data as it is about accounting.

Today the chain exists: an internal core banking ledger we built ourselves, feeding NetSuite, feeding regulatory reporting. What it does not have is a single owner who understands it end-to-end, holds it to the standard a regulated lender needs, and evolves it as the business changes (geographies, products, licenses). That is the role we are opening.

You will join an Accounting team inside a Finance organization of ~15 people covering Strategic Financing, FP&A, Accounting, Regulatory reporting and Controlling. You will report to the Head of Financing & Accounting, alongside the Financing team and the General Accounting Manager, who oversees corporate cycles, tax, statutory and consolidated accounts.

This is a role with unusual ownership for its level: the banking accounting scope is yours from day one, and so is the data chain that produces it.

💼 About the job

Own the accounting of the credit business:

Own how the portfolio is represented in the books: origination, revenue recognition on merchant and customer commissions, deferred income, write-offs and recoveries, cost of risk and provisioning on performing and non-performing exposures.

Own the accounting of our securitizations: sales of receivables to the FCTs, derecognition, discount and over-collateralisation, residual interests, servicing and management fees, hedging.

Own the accounting of our funding: corporate debt, commercial paper, and the new funding instruments we add as the refinancing strategy evolves.

Own the core banking ledger:

Be the functional owner of the engine that turns business events into accounting: which event, which account, which currency, which date, which counterparty.

Specify and validate the accounting schemes for every new product, partner and geography, and work with Engineering and Data on the ledger's model, its feed into the ERP, and the fixes when something drifts.

Own the audit trail end-to-end — from a single €40 installment to a line in a prudential statement — and make it documented enough to be walked through by someone whose job is to challenge it.

Reinforce the control framework:

Design and automate the reconciliations that hold the whole thing together: ledger ↔ general ledger ↔ bank ↔ FCT reporting ↔ prudential statements.

Shorten monthly close, incl. turning a manual, end-of-month, spreadsheet-based check into an automated, evidenced, repeatable control.

Be Finance's counterpart to Internal Control and Periodic Control on everything accounting-data related.

Own regulatory reporting:

Own the production and the quality of our prudential and statistical reporting — solvency, large exposures, liquidity, and the statistical returns that go with them.

Own the reconciliation tables that matter most: prudential statements to accounting balances, regulatory returns to the trial balance, own funds and RWA back to their audit trail.

Own the reporting tooling and its data feeds, and work with the Regulatory and Financing teams on the evolutions of the prudential framework and on the treatment of our securitizations.

🧩 About you

To succeed in this job:

You have around 6-7 years of experience, ideally starting in audit of financial services — banks, consumer credit, asset management, securitization — in a Big 4 or a specialised practice, possibly with a first move in-house. You know how to build a number, prove it, and defend it line by line in front of people whose job is to challenge it.

You know banking accounting for real: French banking GAAP, the PCEC, cost of risk, revenue recognition on credit products. Or you know financial services accounting well enough that the banking layer is a matter of months, not years.

You actually enjoy controls at scale — reconciling large populations, hunting the anomaly, chasing the last twelve euros of a four-hundred-million balance until you know exactly where they went. If that sounds tedious rather than satisfying, this is not your role.

You are autonomous and scrappy. On things to build, or on things that already exist.

You are fluent in English and French — our documentation and our regulator are French, part of our business and our team are not.

And it will be nice if you also:

Hold, or are working towards, the DEC (or CPA, ACCA, equivalent).

Have been exposed to securitization — FCTs, SPVs, waterfalls, deconsolidation — or to a regulated credit institution from the inside.

You are autonomous on data. SQL is a daily tool, a data warehouse does not intimidate you, and your reflex in front of a five-million-row population is to query it, not to ask someone for a summary. This is the single most important line in this job description.

Know NetSuite, BigQuery, dbt or Python.

Have worked in a scaling fintech.

jobs.description:
